newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Senate cuts back budget saving.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Senate cuts back budget saving.

text.p: The Australian Senate rejected part of the government's budget on Thursday, refusing to tighten eligibility for a tax break on research and development as far as the government wanted.

The biggest doubtful measure in the government's tax bill survived the Senate, but the upper house cut back a policy to exclude syndicates from the R&D tax break, which would have saved A$170 million in the fiscal year to June 1998 had it survived untouched.

The Senate determined that partnerships would keep the tax break as syndicates. No estimate was available of the fiscal impact of the change, which would be some part of the full A$170 million value of the measure.
The Senate had not finished consideration of the entire tax bill, which contains other measures, when it adjourned at 1300 GMT (midnight AEDT).
Earlier, the Senate passed a larger R&D measure in the budget -- reducing the strength of the tax break by cutting the tax deductability for R&D spending to 125 percent from 150 percent.
The government estimated that this alone was worth A$430 million to the budget in 1997/98, its first full year of operation.
The measures are part of a budget tightening announced in August that was supposed to cut the 1997/98 budget by A$7.2 billion.

About A$2.0 billion of that tightening became doubtful in the weeks following the budget as minority parties declared their opposition. Most of the remaing doubtful measures will be determined by Senate votes on Friday.
